note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer diagnosis following histological progression on repeat biopsy.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 68-year-old delivery driver, never married, living alone with his adult son as primary contact. He has a history of obesity (BMI >30), although his current BMI is 22.3. He is a non-smoker, consumes 3 units of alcohol per week, and exercises by walking 45 minutes daily. His IPSS score is 12/35, indicating moderate lower urinary tract symptoms. He has had recent appointments with cardiology (stable, autumn 2024), physiotherapy for lower back pain (six sessions), and a baseline screening at the memory clinic. He has no active medications and no known allergies.
On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with cT1c staging. General examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs including blood pressure of 138/81 mmHg and heart rate of 68 bpm.
